name: Places (general)
author: Molfar
description: Generic places for stories across fantasy, science fiction, modern, historical and horror settings.

entries.name: Lantern Stair
entries.desc: A spiral staircase cut into a sea cliff, lit by thousands of glass lanterns tended by hermits. Each lantern holds a traveler's promise to come back.

entries.name: Hollow of Small Bells
entries.desc: A forest glen where bells hang from every branch and ring only when someone nearby is lying. Locals learn to speak in whispers.

entries.name: Saltmarrow Ferry
entries.desc: A ferry poled across a river of brine by a patient giant tortoise. The fare is one memory of the sea.

entries.name: Tallow Spire
entries.desc: A tower built from melted candle wax over centuries and still warm to the touch. Its walls repeat the last words spoken near them.

entries.name: Gloamwick Market
entries.desc: A market held only at dusk beneath nets of living glowworms, where stalls trade in borrowed shadows and bottled weather.

entries.name: The Stilted Court
entries.desc: A royal court on tall wooden stilts above a flooding plain. Its nobles swear never to touch the ground.

entries.name: Pennywhistle Gorge
entries.desc: A narrow canyon where wind plays the rock like a flute. Travelers navigate by the tune and the tune changes daily.

entries.name: Orchard of Seven Winters
entries.desc: An orchard where each tree bears fruit of a different frost. A bite brings back one winter you once lived through.

entries.name: Brindlecomb
entries.desc: A village of beekeepers who use honey as coin and trained bees as couriers. Strangers are paid in stings first.

entries.name: Kettle Hill Observatory
entries.desc: A copper-domed observatory that tracks stars no one else can see. Its keeper trades star charts for hot soup.

entries.name: Underglass Gardens
entries.desc: Terraced gardens grown beneath a lake of clear ice, lit by pale sun and tended by divers in waxed coats.

entries.name: The Sleeping Colossus Quarter
entries.desc: A district built along the back of a sleeping giant. Tenants plan rent around its slow breathing.

entries.name: Whistlestop Cairn
entries.desc: A crossroads marked by a tall pile of stones, each left by a traveler who made a wish. Some stones hum at night.

entries.name: Marrowmere
entries.desc: A milky lake said to be fed by the bones of an ancient beast. Fishers pull up carved ivory instead of fish.

entries.name: Tidewright's Yard
entries.desc: A shipyard that builds vessels meant to sail rivers in the sky. Its shipwrights never say who ordered them.

entries.name: Cinderfen
entries.desc: A smoldering peat bog where warm mist rises year round. Wild fire-sprites nest in its hollow logs.

entries.name: Vellum Reach
entries.desc: A scholars' island where books grow like fruit on pale trees. Unripe volumes are forbidden to read.

entries.name: Hobnail Bridge
entries.desc: A narrow stone bridge guarded by a courteous troll who collects tolls in riddles and sends no one away hungry.

entries.name: Quillfeather Roost
entries.desc: A tall cliff-top dovecote where messenger birds from every land come to rest. Its keeper reads all the letters.

entries.name: Ambergate
entries.desc: A city gate sealed long ago in a block of amber. The guards inside still stand watch, faintly moving.

entries.name: The Inn at Three Roads
entries.desc: An inn where each of three doors opens onto a different road. Guests sometimes leave by the wrong one.

entries.name: Thistledown Moor
entries.desc: A windy upland of drifting seed and low stone huts. Folk here sell weather forecasts read from fluff.

entries.name: Mirrorpool Cloister
entries.desc: A silent cloister around a pool that shows not faces but the choices a person nearly made.

entries.name: Drowsy Mile
entries.desc: A stretch of road where travelers grow sleepy and must be walked through by awake guides for a small fee.

entries.name: Copperleaf Terraces
entries.desc: Hillside terraces where trees with copper foliage chime softly. Their leaves are minted into the local coin.

entries.name: Greywether Fair
entries.desc: A traveling fair held on the back of a vast flock of sheep that wanders the downs. Stalls are moved by shepherds.

entries.name: Needle Isle
entries.desc: A thin island with one tall spire, home to tailors who stitch maps into cloth and sell them as cloaks.

entries.name: Cairn of Lost Names
entries.desc: A field of flat stones, each carved with a name nobody remembers. Visitors may take one if they leave their own.

entries.name: Foxglove Ford
entries.desc: A shallow river crossing ringed with purple blossoms. Those who wade it speak truthfully until they reach the far bank.

entries.name: The Weaver's Descent
entries.desc: A mine where thread, not ore, is drawn from the rock in glinting strands. Miners spin as they climb.

entries.name: Gallowmere
entries.desc: A drowned village where the church spire still pokes from the black water. Fishermen swear the bell tolls for the dead below.

entries.name: The Thorn Reliquary
entries.desc: A cathedral grown entirely from briars, its saints' bones woven into the walls. Every thorn bleeds if cut.

entries.name: Cold Hearth Keep
entries.desc: A fortress whose fires never warm anyone. Its lords sit in furs and speak in clouds of breath.

entries.name: Ashen Ossuary
entries.desc: A catacomb whose bones have been sorted by trade and rank, as though the dead still held office.

entries.name: Widowmoor
entries.desc: A sodden heath crossed by a single raised road. Every stranger found on it is said to belong to somebody who waits.

entries.name: The Hanging Orchard
entries.desc: A grove where fruit trees bear nooses in place of branches. The fruit is eaten by the bold and the desperate.

entries.name: Mourner's Quay
entries.desc: A stone dock where the dead are set afloat in black skiffs and paid mourners wail for hire.

entries.name: Sootbell Abbey
entries.desc: A ruined abbey whose bell tolls under its own power and whose monks vanished mid-prayer. Candles still burn.

entries.name: The Rotting Court
entries.desc: A king's hall whose banquet table is never cleared. Courtiers eat spoiled feasts and call it tradition.

entries.name: Carrion Hill
entries.desc: A bare rise where large black birds gather in orderly rows. Local judges read the birds before sentencing.

entries.name: Hollowgrave
entries.desc: A cemetery with open graves on every plot, waiting. Gravediggers refuse to say who they are dug for.

entries.name: Bleak Anvil
entries.desc: A smithy-town where iron is forged from the tears of captives. Its blades never rust and never forgive.

entries.name: The Gaunt Bridge
entries.desc: A bridge of fused ribs spanning a bottomless gorge. Travelers who cross it count their ribs for days after.

entries.name: Vesper Lazaret
entries.desc: A hospital for the cursed, run by nuns in veils. The wards fill silently and are never emptied.

entries.name: Sallow Gate
entries.desc: The sickly yellow gate of a plague city, locked from within. A hand-painted sign asks visitors to leave bread.

entries.name: The Choir of Stones
entries.desc: A circle of standing stones that sing in grief when someone is about to die.

entries.name: Wormwood Deep
entries.desc: A tidal cave where bitter herbs grow on drowned things. Hags harvest them for potions that make victims forget.

entries.name: Blighted Furrow
entries.desc: A field that swallowed its last harvest and sprouted teeth. Farmers still plant it by decree.

entries.name: Marrow Market
entries.desc: A butcher's square where odd cuts are sold from covered carts. Buyers ask no questions and sellers offer none.

entries.name: Dirge Landing
entries.desc: A harbor where only funeral ships dock. The sea outside it is never calm.

entries.name: The Silent Archive
entries.desc: A vault of sealed confessions, each stamped with a wax seal that is warm to the touch.

entries.name: Hunger Hall
entries.desc: A lord's banquet hall where plates are always set and never filled. The ghosts there bite.

entries.name: The Pale Chapel
entries.desc: A white chapel under a sky that never changes color. Those who pray inside forget what they asked for.

entries.name: Gravewrought Mine
entries.desc: A mine where the ore is bone-pale and cold. Miners hear their own voices speaking from deeper galleries.

entries.name: Haunted Tithe Barn
entries.desc: A great barn where the harvest tithe is paid in years of life, collected by clerks without faces.

entries.name: Briar Court
entries.desc: A walled garden where roses grow over the sleepers who tended them. Pruning is forbidden.

entries.name: Umber Fen
entries.desc: A brown marsh of drifting lights that lead travelers into the mud. Some lights are friendly. Most are not.

entries.name: Crook's Rest
entries.desc: A gallows hill where every post bears a lantern for the hanged. After midnight the lanterns swing together.

entries.name: Scarlet Maw
entries.desc: A crater in the mountains that opens like a mouth in the thaw. Pilgrims toss in their sins and sometimes hear thanks.

entries.name: Hollow Saint's Rest
entries.desc: A shrine to a saint whose statue is hollow and filled with whispers. Pilgrims press their ear to its cracks.

entries.name: Kepler Ring Habitat
entries.desc: A rotating orbital ring whose residents farm on the inner surface under artificial dusk. Weather is voted on monthly.

entries.name: Cold Dock Nine
entries.desc: A freight dock on a frozen moon where ships wait weeks for ice to be cut. Gossip is the main currency.

entries.name: Lattice Station
entries.desc: A research station built as an open scaffold around a drifting singularity. Staff pay in time dilation.

entries.name: The Long Garden
entries.desc: A hydroponic spine running the length of a generation ship, tended by caretakers who never meet anyone from the far end.

entries.name: Halcyon Basin
entries.desc: A terraformed crater with real rain and a dome that mimics seasons. Tourists book years ahead.

entries.name: Quiet Relay
entries.desc: A communications platform at the edge of a system where signals arrive older than they should. Its operators keep a diary of echoes.

entries.name: Redshift Bazaar
entries.desc: A market that drifts between stars on a retired hauler. Prices change with the ship's speed.

entries.name: Orchard World Prime
entries.desc: A planet turned into a single enormous orchard, picked by drones and ferried by tall cargo balloons.

entries.name: Pale Observatory
entries.desc: A deep-space telescope station staffed by monks of data who log every flicker and rarely speak aloud.

entries.name: Tin Cathedral
entries.desc: A reused ship hull converted into a chapel for those who pray to the engines. Its choir is a bank of idling turbines.

entries.name: Meridian Gantry
entries.desc: A launch tower on a tidally locked world, standing on the thin ring of habitable twilight.

entries.name: The Ballast Vault
entries.desc: A hollow asteroid where lost cargo of dead ships is stored. Salvagers bid by lantern light.

entries.name: Sable Reach
entries.desc: A dark nebula outpost with no windows facing out, where residents trust only instruments.

entries.name: Thistle Station
entries.desc: A mining platform shaped like a spiked ball that spins to keep dust off its drills.

entries.name: Obol Clearing
entries.desc: A neutral docking zone where rival fleets trade under a truce enforced by an old automated referee.

entries.name: Evenfall Array
entries.desc: A field of tall solar masts on a desert world that bow in unison when the sun sets.

entries.name: The Cradle Archive
entries.desc: A vault holding frozen embryos and seed stock for a hundred worlds. Its overseer is a patient, tired machine.

entries.name: Ice Chorus
entries.desc: A drifting comet colony whose frozen halls sing when heated by passing sunlight.

entries.name: Vagrant's Elevator
entries.desc: A space elevator whose cabins are rented by the hour. Passengers argue over the view.

entries.name: Brass Meridian
entries.desc: A retro-styled starport that deliberately uses mechanical instruments and clerks with stamps.

entries.name: Gantry Eleven
entries.desc: An abandoned shipyard where half-built hulls hang in the dark like unfinished fish.

entries.name: Stillwater Deep
entries.desc: An ocean world habitat whose glass domes sit on stilts above a rolling sea of heavy water.

entries.name: The Sieve
entries.desc: A customs checkpoint that sifts every arriving ship through nested scanners. Smugglers say it blinks.

entries.name: Hollow Moon Spa
entries.desc: A resort carved inside a small moon, offering low gravity soaks to the wealthy and weary.

entries.name: Marrow Station
entries.desc: A waste-processing platform whose crews salvage useful junk from the discarded. The smell is legendary.

entries.name: Wren Platform
entries.desc: A tiny listening post run by two technicians who speak to whales through drifting buoys.

entries.name: Seed Vault Sigma
entries.desc: A bunker orbiting a dead planet, stocked with life samples and a hesitant caretaker program.

entries.name: Longshot Depot
entries.desc: A fuel stop on a route so long that crews age between visits. Its barkeep remembers everyone.

entries.name: Parallax Court
entries.desc: A floating tribunal where cases from far colonies are tried with a seven-minute delay between questions.

entries.name: Glasswright Orbital
entries.desc: A factory ring that spins fine lenses and crystals for the nearest dozen worlds.

entries.name: Late Night Laundromat
entries.desc: A fluorescent laundromat open twenty-four hours where regulars trade stories over spinning drums. Its owner never seems to sleep.

entries.name: Parking Level Six
entries.desc: The top deck of an empty garage, used by skateboarders and nervous couples. The lights flicker in a pattern.

entries.name: Nine Lives Pet Shop
entries.desc: A cramped pet shop whose owner talks to the animals. Customers leave with companions rather than purchases.

entries.name: Alder Street Diner
entries.desc: A railcar diner with cracked red booths and bottomless coffee. The waitress has heard every confession.

entries.name: Rooftop Allotment
entries.desc: A community garden on a flat roof above a shopping arcade. Tenants guard their tomatoes with suspicion.

entries.name: Terminal C Chapel
entries.desc: A tiny interfaith prayer room tucked in an airport. Delayed travelers wander in and linger.

entries.name: Corner Copy Shop
entries.desc: A print shop with a broken scanner and an owner who files everyone's lost items.

entries.name: Pedestrian Overpass
entries.desc: A graffiti-covered footbridge above a six-lane road, where people stop to watch evening traffic.

entries.name: The Basement Arcade
entries.desc: A damp arcade of old cabinets run by a former champion. High scores are guarded like family secrets.

entries.name: Wet Market Row
entries.desc: An open-air market of fish, spice and live poultry that wakes at four every morning.

entries.name: Harbor View Laundry Steps
entries.desc: Concrete steps beside the port where dockworkers' families hang washing. Gulls take the best seats.

entries.name: Greyfield Reservoir
entries.desc: A fenced reservoir with a jogging path. Joggers say the surface sometimes shows a different sky.

entries.name: Evening Ferry Landing
entries.desc: A small wooden landing where commuters wait for the last boat. Strangers share umbrellas.

entries.name: Seventh Floor Records Office
entries.desc: A municipal office with endless forms and one friendly clerk who knows where everything is filed.

entries.name: The Quiet Car
entries.desc: A train compartment where talking is forbidden and everyone has secrets. Regulars sit in the same seats.

entries.name: Greenhouse Cafe
entries.desc: A cafe inside a derelict glass conservatory. Plants grow through the chairs and the menu changes with the harvest.

entries.name: Underpass Gallery
entries.desc: A tunnel under a rail line where local painters hang work on the walls overnight and take it down by dawn.

entries.name: Old Pool Hall
entries.desc: A hall with sticky floors and a ceiling fan that turns once a minute. Regulars still keep chalk in their pockets.

entries.name: Radio Tower Hill
entries.desc: A hill with an abandoned broadcast tower where teenagers go to talk and look at the city.

entries.name: Marigold Block
entries.desc: An apartment complex with a shared courtyard and a long-standing feud over the clothesline.

entries.name: The Lost Property Depot
entries.desc: A warehouse of items left on buses and trains. Staff keep rare treasures and unclaimed letters in a drawer.

entries.name: Night Bus Terminus
entries.desc: An empty bus station lit by one vending machine. Late arrivals share its warmth and the driver's stories.

entries.name: Suburban Cul-de-sac
entries.desc: A circular street of identical houses where every porch light is on a timer, and the neighbors keep close watch.

entries.name: Fourth Street Barbershop
entries.desc: A two-chair shop where news is traded faster than haircuts. The owner insists on cash.

entries.name: Seaside Arcade Pier
entries.desc: A sagging pier of lights and sticky floors, closed in winter, haunted in summer by teenage crushes.

entries.name: Hospital Garden
entries.desc: A courtyard behind a clinic where patients and visitors sit among planter boxes and sometimes tell the truth.

entries.name: Corporate Atrium
entries.desc: A glass lobby with a fountain and an overworked receptionist who knows every executive's real habits.

entries.name: Rain Check Bar
entries.desc: A narrow bar open only during storms. Its regulars arrive soaked and unusually honest.

entries.name: The Short Stay Hotel
entries.desc: A budget hotel with thin walls and a night manager who keeps a list of strange guests.

entries.name: Overnight Library
entries.desc: A branch library kept open all night by a stubborn librarian. Students and insomniacs share its tables.

entries.name: Neon Alley 9
entries.desc: A narrow lane of glowing signs and noodle stalls above a drain. Every sign sells something illegal in code.

entries.name: Rust Canal Hub
entries.desc: A flooded intersection where drone barges trade scrap and chips. The water runs oily and warm.

entries.name: The Wire Garden
entries.desc: A rooftop of tangled cables and potted bonsai, tended by a hacker who prunes both.

entries.name: Chrome Row Clinic
entries.desc: A back-room clinic that installs cheap implants. Its sign says sterile, its smell says otherwise.

entries.name: Lowtide Arcade
entries.desc: A basement arcade where players bet their reflexes and sometimes their implants.

entries.name: Static District
entries.desc: A neighborhood with no signal because of a jammer an angry landlord installed. It has become a refuge.

entries.name: Gutter Exchange
entries.desc: An underground market that trades in leaked data and stolen memories, run from a shuttered subway car.

entries.name: Hazard Row Noodles
entries.desc: A street kitchen under a flickering awning, serving soup with extra voltage. Customers eat standing up.

entries.name: The Sump
entries.desc: A sewer-level slum of repurposed server racks, where hackers sleep in cold cabinets and trade scraps.

entries.name: Glass Needle Tower
entries.desc: A corporate tower with mirrored windows and sub-floors the maps do not list. Drone swarms circle at night.

entries.name: Burnout Lane
entries.desc: A dead-end street of closed bars where ex-runners drink alone and recall the old jobs.

entries.name: Halogen Hotel
entries.desc: A capsule hotel stacked fourteen stories high, rented by the hour. Rooms are tracked by ceiling cameras.

entries.name: Servo Yard
entries.desc: A scrapyard of discarded androids and exoskeletons. Parts are sorted by size, not sorrow.

entries.name: Pachinko Spire
entries.desc: A vertical casino stacked above a shopping mall, dazzling in colors that hurt to look at.

entries.name: Overpass Shrine
entries.desc: A small shrine tucked under a highway, offerings of cheap chips and battery packs left for lost data-ghosts.

entries.name: Datashrine Seven
entries.desc: A server farm turned temple where believers upload prayers to a patient system.

entries.name: Smog Level Mall
entries.desc: A mall on the permanently hazy ground floor, selling air filters, replacement eyes and cheap luck.

entries.name: Backdoor Ramen
entries.desc: A ramen bar behind a locked door with a rotating password. Fixers, thieves and cops all eat there.

entries.name: Tangle Market
entries.desc: A street market under tangled power lines, where vendors tap electricity and each other.

entries.name: Ghost Line Station
entries.desc: An abandoned maglev station where signal-ghosts of commuters repeat their routes on cracked screens.

entries.name: Amber Alley Clinic
entries.desc: A clinic for virtual addiction, tucked beside a bar. Patients check in under assumed names.

entries.name: Lag Town
entries.desc: A district served by obsolete networks, always a few seconds behind everyone else. It has its own slang.

entries.name: The Fixer's Roof
entries.desc: A rooftop shack with a satellite dish and a bar made of mismatched crates. Jobs are posted by ribbon.

entries.name: Brownout Block
entries.desc: A tenement where the power cuts out at a set hour. Residents bribe the grid to keep the lights on.

entries.name: Mirror Level
entries.desc: A floor of a megatower papered with advertisements that react to onlookers' moods.

entries.name: Kilowatt Chapel
entries.desc: A chapel in a transformer station where technicians pray before shifts. Candles are forbidden, so they use LEDs.

entries.name: Pawn & Patch
entries.desc: A shop offering loans against organs and firmware. It always has a queue of regulars.

entries.name: Neon Mortuary
entries.desc: A glowing morgue that scans and uploads the dead. Relatives pay by the megabyte.

entries.name: Ferrous Bay
entries.desc: A harbor of automated cranes that never sleep. A single human supervisor keeps a mug and a prayer.

entries.name: The Under-Level Garden
entries.desc: A hidden greenhouse beneath a power plant, lit by grow lamps and guarded by a retired courier.

entries.name: Rust Harbor
entries.desc: A shipyard of rotting hulls turned into a trading post. Traders barter fuel and clean water at fixed ranks.

entries.name: The Dry Reservoir
entries.desc: A dried-out reservoir whose floor has become a market. Stalls are set where the old waterline once ran.

entries.name: Cinder Orchard
entries.desc: A burnt orchard where ash-black trees still bear sour fruit. Wanderers camp there for the shade.

entries.name: Chime Ridge
entries.desc: A ridge strung with wind chimes made of cans and cutlery. Raiders know to avoid it.

entries.name: Last Fuel Pump
entries.desc: A single working gas station run by a stubborn attendant who refuses to open for raiders.

entries.name: Bunker Eleven
entries.desc: A cramped underground shelter run by a council who keep the door shut and the ledgers tidy.

entries.name: The Greenhouse Mile
entries.desc: A mile of connected greenhouses, patched with plastic and glue, feeding a thriving settlement.

entries.name: Scrapwright Fair
entries.desc: A seasonal market of tinkers and mechanics trading salvaged machines. Prices are set by bartering contests.

entries.name: Glasslands
entries.desc: A plain fused to glass by an old blast. Its surface cuts boots but sparkles under sunset.

entries.name: Sandcrawler Depot
entries.desc: A caravan stop built inside a stranded pipeline carrier. Drivers pay in water and gossip.

entries.name: Mirror Dam
entries.desc: A cracked dam whose spillway still holds a reflective lake. Scavengers say the fish glow.

entries.name: Tin Roof Town
entries.desc: A settlement of metal sheets and shared walls, lit at night by oil lamps and quarrels.

entries.name: The Lantern Road
entries.desc: A highway where survivors place lit lamps to guide travelers at night. Breaking one earns exile.

entries.name: Hollow Mall
entries.desc: A collapsed shopping center full of looted shops and families who sleep in dressing rooms.

entries.name: Brine Flats
entries.desc: A salt desert of dry lake beds. Salt-cutters sell blocks to anyone with a mule.

entries.name: Pump House Rest
entries.desc: A well-guarded pump house where caravans pay a cup per head. Its water tastes of copper.

entries.name: Ember Silo
entries.desc: A grain silo turned into a defended farm, with ladders hidden and a dog on every platform.

entries.name: The Windmill Line
entries.desc: A row of old turbines that still turn, each claimed by a family who trade power for protection.

entries.name: Overpass Bazaar
entries.desc: A market in the shade of a collapsed highway. Merchants pay a lookout for every cloud of dust.

entries.name: Dustwater Station
entries.desc: A rail stop where the last working train arrives once a month. Locals have a feast every time.

entries.name: Seedkeeper's Yard
entries.desc: A fenced garden where heirloom seeds are traded under armed guard and dim lamps.

entries.name: Rubble Harbor
entries.desc: A port in a drowned city where boats dock at the tops of buildings.

entries.name: The Last School
entries.desc: A school in a freight car where a retired teacher keeps a chalkboard and fourteen students.

entries.name: Gauge Hill
entries.desc: A hilltop with an old weather station whose keeper sells forecasts and warnings.

entries.name: Cairn Camp
entries.desc: A rest stop of stacked stones and tarps, where wanderers leave messages for those behind.

entries.name: Ruin Library
entries.desc: A half-burnt library whose librarian guards what is left and barters knowledge for food.

entries.name: The Long Quarantine
entries.desc: A fenced district kept in isolation for generations, now a tight and odd community.

entries.name: Gravel Mouth
entries.desc: A quarry pit turned into a fortress, with ladders that vanish at night.

entries.name: Shipwreck Row
entries.desc: A line of beached cargo ships turned into homes, linked by rope bridges and loud rumor.

entries.name: Moth Light Camp
entries.desc: A caravan camp lit by hanging lamps that draw clouds of moths. Travelers say it feels like a feast.

entries.name: Cobbler's Row
entries.desc: A narrow lane of leather workers, where apprentices shout at passersby and the smell of tanned hide hangs thick.

entries.name: The Wool Staple Hall
entries.desc: A merchants' hall where wool is weighed and sealed under watchful eyes of guild officials.

entries.name: Millers' Bridge
entries.desc: A covered timber bridge with shops along both sides. Fire drills are strictly enforced.

entries.name: Tollhouse at the Ford
entries.desc: A small stone tollhouse where a clerk records every cart and keeps a ledger of travelers' complaints.

entries.name: Brewers' Guildhall
entries.desc: A hall with long tables, a heavy beam ceiling and a tradition of settling disputes over ale.

entries.name: The Drovers' Inn
entries.desc: An inn on a cattle road with a muddy yard and shared beds, famous for its pea soup and its fiddlers.

entries.name: Salt Pans
entries.desc: Shallow evaporation ponds along a coast, worked by families who sell their yield by cartload.

entries.name: Frostfair Common
entries.desc: A common where a frozen river hosts a winter fair, with stalls set directly on the ice.

entries.name: Lamplighter's Lane
entries.desc: A street where a guild of lamplighters trims wicks each dusk. Their ladders lean on every post.

entries.name: The Scriveners' Yard
entries.desc: A courtyard of public letter writers who draft contracts and love notes for a few coins.

entries.name: Hillfort Stockade
entries.desc: A timber palisade on a hilltop, home to a small clan and a great many dogs.

entries.name: Dyers' Quay
entries.desc: A riverside row where cloth dyers rinse bright cloth, staining the water in changing colors.

entries.name: Granary Square
entries.desc: A square dominated by a stone granary, the site of grain markets and public announcements.

entries.name: The Court Leet
entries.desc: A rural court meeting under an oak where villagers argue over boundaries and stray pigs.

entries.name: Pilgrims' Hospice
entries.desc: A hostel on a pilgrim road, run by monks, offering a bed and a bowl for a prayer.

entries.name: The Ropewalk
entries.desc: A very long shed where rope makers walk backwards spinning hemp into cable.

entries.name: Caravanserai of the Plain
entries.desc: A walled inn for desert travelers, with a central well and stalls for camels.

entries.name: Harbourmaster's Office
entries.desc: A harbor building with a high window and a ledger of every ship, kept by a sharp-eyed official.

entries.name: Lockkeeper's Cottage
entries.desc: A small house by a canal lock, where the keeper watches barges and trades in local rumor.

entries.name: Pewterers' Hall
entries.desc: A craft hall where pewter is cast and tested. Its marks were considered binding in disputes.

entries.name: Warning Knoll
entries.desc: A hill with a stack of wood ready for the alarm. Watchmen draw lots for the lonely night shift.

entries.name: The Hiring Fair
entries.desc: A square where servants and laborers stand in rows holding tokens of their trades, hoping for a master.

entries.name: Quarantine Island
entries.desc: A small island where arriving ships wait out forty days before landing. Its chapel has no bell.

entries.name: Powder Mill
entries.desc: A stone mill by a stream, where gunpowder is mixed in cautious batches and visitors surrender their boots.

entries.name: Bellfounders' Yard
entries.desc: A yard where bronze bells are cast, and each new bell is named by the village that orders it.

entries.name: Pigeon Post Station
entries.desc: A tower of nesting boxes where pigeons carry messages for merchants and spies alike.

entries.name: Almshouse Court
entries.desc: A court of tiny cottages for retired workers, with a gate-keeper who counts the visitors.

entries.name: Cartographers' Loft
entries.desc: An attic where mapmakers copy charts by candlelight, drawing in empty regions with sea monsters.

entries.name: Garrison Fort at the Pass
entries.desc: A stone fort commanding a mountain pass, drafty, poorly supplied and fiercely loyal.

entries.name: The Candle Fair
entries.desc: A winter fair where tallow and wax are sold by weight, and children are given small stubs to light the dark.

entries.name: Hollow Pines Lodge
entries.desc: A remote lodge where guests are checked in but never recorded leaving. The wallpaper is slightly different each morning.

entries.name: The Third Stair
entries.desc: A basement staircase that has one more step every time you walk down.

entries.name: Wickfield Farmhouse
entries.desc: A farm with a locked cellar and a family that dines at a table set for one extra.

entries.name: Dead Channel Studio
entries.desc: A closed television studio whose set lights still warm up at night, and whose audience is invisible.

entries.name: Murmur Lane
entries.desc: A quiet street where every window shows a faint figure watching. Mailboxes contain unsigned letters.

entries.name: Sister Agnes Orphanage
entries.desc: A shuttered orphanage with a playroom of cold toys. Children's laughter drifts down the stairs.

entries.name: Nowhere Motel
entries.desc: A roadside motel with no road behind it. The vacancy sign flickers in a pattern.

entries.name: The Stairwell Between Floors
entries.desc: A fire stair where doors open onto floors that do not exist in the building plan.

entries.name: Whisper Marsh
entries.desc: A fog-bound fen where voices of the missing call from the reeds, perfectly mimicking loved ones.

entries.name: Lamplit Asylum
entries.desc: A decommissioned asylum with the lamps still burning. Staff files describe patients who were never admitted.

entries.name: Candlewick Funeral Home
entries.desc: A parlor where the dead are laid out for visitors who never come. The embalmer smiles too widely.

entries.name: The Last Carriage
entries.desc: The final car of a night train where passengers sit in silence. Those who fall asleep wake at an unknown station.

entries.name: Cellar of Birthdays
entries.desc: A basement room full of dusty cakes with candles for every year of a stranger's life.

entries.name: Greywater Reservoir
entries.desc: A drained reservoir whose bottom reveals an entire village. Something still tends its wells.

entries.name: The Photographer's Studio
entries.desc: A studio where portraits come back with one extra figure in the background.

entries.name: Ravel Street Theater
entries.desc: A theater whose velvet curtain rises on its own. The play is always the audience's last evening.

entries.name: Thistle Well
entries.desc: A deep well that echoes with answers before the question is spoken. Children are forbidden to lean over it.

entries.name: The Parish of Quiet
entries.desc: A chapel village where the residents never speak after dusk and their eyes follow strangers.

entries.name: Birchwood Sanatorium
entries.desc: A mountain sanatorium that treats a cough with long rests and unplanned disappearances.

entries.name: Pennyfarthing Carnival
entries.desc: An out-of-season carnival where carousels turn alone and the ticket seller never looks up.

entries.name: Nightshift Hospital Wing
entries.desc: A closed ward where the intercom still calls for doctors who retired decades ago.

entries.name: Barrow Field
entries.desc: A barrow field where grass grows in the shapes of faces. Farmers plough around them.

entries.name: Lullaby Manor
entries.desc: A decaying mansion where a music box plays by itself each midnight. The nursery is always warm.

entries.name: Elm Hollow Schoolhouse
entries.desc: A one-room school where the roll call includes names that nobody recognizes.

entries.name: The Meat Locker
entries.desc: A walk-in freezer at a closed butcher's that hums with an odd tune. Its door has no inside handle.

entries.name: Cinder Road Tunnel
entries.desc: A railway tunnel that is longer on the way out. Drivers who stop their engines hear knocking.

entries.name: Gravel Pit Lake
entries.desc: A flooded quarry where swimmers feel hands around their ankles. Rescue divers refuse to go deeper.

entries.name: The Waiting Room
entries.desc: A clinic with one chair too many and a receptionist who calls numbers nobody holds.

entries.name: Larder of the Old Hall
entries.desc: A cold pantry in a derelict hall, stocked with preserves labeled in a child's hand with names of the missing.

entries.name: Bellweather Fairground
entries.desc: A fairground where the fortune teller's booth has a sign reading closed. Someone still answers.
